public_rationale: The arithmetic holds. 15.5 million paid subscribers at the end of 2024 (e1) divided by his upper estimate of 600 million monthly users is 2.583%. Calling that 'astonishingly bad' is his opinion and is not graded. The universal cost claim is only partly backed. Altman said OpenAI lost money on $200 Pro subscriptions (e2), so some paying users did cost more than they paid. But The Information reported that at the end of 2024, OpenAI kept about 52% of paying-user revenue after the cost of running models for those users (e3). On that measure, paying users as a group more than covered what it cost to serve them, which contradicts 'every single user, regardless of whether they pay'. Free users were not tested.
limitations: The compute margin is an internal measure from an unnamed source, and OpenAI did not confirm it.
If 'loses money' means a fully loaded share of training and overhead costs, no public per-user data settles it.
The conversion rate rests on his own MAU estimate, which cannot be checked.

For paying users, the closest public measure is revenue minus the cost of running models for those users.
